title_en: The man who passed by a ruined town
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The town and the hundred years

claims.statement_en: The Quran gives the case of one who passed by a town that had fallen in ruins over its roofs, and he asked how God would give it life after its death.
God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him.
He was asked how long he had stayed, and he said a day or part of a day, and he was told that he had stayed a hundred years.

He was told to look at his food and drink, which had not spoiled, and at his donkey, so that God might make him a sign for the people, and to look at the bones, how God sets them together and then clothes them with flesh.
When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things.

chapters.summary_md: A man passed by a town that had fallen in ruins and asked how God would give it life after its death [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.body_md: The Quran gives the case of one who passed by a town that had fallen in ruins over its roofs, and he asked how God would give it life after its death [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. He was asked how long he had stayed, and he said a day or part of a day, and he was told that he had stayed a hundred years [c3]. He was told to look at his food and drink, which had not spoiled, and at his donkey, so that God might make him a sign for the people, and to look at the bones, how God sets them together and then clothes them with flesh [c4]. When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name the man or the town [c1]. It does not say who asked him how long he had stayed [c3]. The Arabic for how God sets the bones together is read in more than one way in the recitations [c4].
chapters.kids_md: A man passed by a town that had fallen in ruins [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. He thought he had stayed a day or part of a day, and was told that it was a hundred years [c3]. He said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the man's question about the town is answered by what happened to him [c1][c2]. Another is that his last words are a statement that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the man's name, his faith or whether he was a prophet; the ayah calls him one who passed by a town.
- Not established: the name of the town, or who destroyed it.
- Not established: who asked him how long he had stayed; the ayah does not name the speaker.
- Not established: what the sign for the people was, beyond the words of the ayah.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man and the town are identified in later works.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is identified as Uzayr or as another figure, and the town as Jerusalem; the text itself names neither.
Hadith to add later: reports about the man who passed by the town, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
